# Research question

When do thermodynamic and interphase-model choices change predicted capture and
axial temperature, and which numerical methods resolve those changes efficiently?
The submitted revision is preserved separately. This notebook organizes retained
findings and possible next studies; no new column calculation was performed during
branch consolidation.

# Select the calculation explicitly

A study TOML file selects a formulation, thermodynamic model, film closure,
method, cases and numerical settings. Preview prints the selection without
importing the model. Execution requires `--run` and a new output directory.

```bash
python3 src/mea_absorption_column/research.py --list-options
python3 src/mea_absorption_column/research.py analyses/research_options/options.toml
```

| Formulation | Implemented selections | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Seven-state column | Henry, neutral/ionic ePC-SAFT or nine-species reactive ePC-SAFT; explicit/implicit enhancement or supplied film linearization; shooting, SciPy BVP or finite differences | Existing column balances and empirical calorics, with explicitly selected closures |
| Conserved balances supplied by a study | Trapezoidal, centered, shooting or adaptive collocation | The builder supplies compatible thermodynamics, film, balances and boundaries; a method change need not change those equations |
| Twelve-state conserved column | `reactive_epcsaft`, equilibrium-manifold or enhancement reference; trapezoidal, central or upwind CasADi/IPOPT | Integrated preset with native total enthalpy and hydraulic pressure drop; see the bounded capability evidence below |

A linearized film profile is a frozen input to an outer iteration. It is not a
solved film at every new column state. Native derivatives currently cover the
explicit-enhancement seven-state path; unsupported derivative combinations fail
rather than masquerade as an exact Jacobian. Estimated parameters and preliminary
methods remain usable research topics without being labelled validated.

# Retained findings and potential promotions

| Study | Retained finding | Next discriminating work |
|---|---|---|
| Submitted nine-species column | Seven-case evaluation, Case 3C refinement and sensitivity studies are retained on `codex/fallback-manuscript` | Use as a stated reference when relevant; it does not define every research case |
| Equilibrium-manifold film campaign | Film capture MAE 6.700 percentage points versus 4.038 for its enhancement comparator; estimated mobility and mixed bulk/film changes limit interpretation | Separate bulk-thermodynamic changes from film changes on common inputs before attributing improvement |
| Film numerical reachability | One provisional state completed after 592.179 s, six iterations and 355 points; kinetics/diffusivities were unresolved | Resolve physical inputs before interpreting the computed flux as an experimental prediction |
| CasADi RHS comparison | A value-only callback did not supply the required total derivative; disposable finite-difference trials did not establish the target speedup | Use an explicitly differentiable formulation; compare cost at matched numerical accuracy |
| Conservative-method development | Analytic checks and consistent single-node recovery are retained; a full-column method ranking is absent | Establish a coherent coupled builder and converged trajectory before a physical timing/refinement comparison |
| MDEA and eNRTL | MDEA interface groundwork is retained, but neither is an integrated selectable column model here | Supply equations, parameter/reaction bases and mapped observations before claiming a comparable model |

# Comparison design

Change one specified closure at a time when interpreting its effect. Compare
common feed bases, geometry, transport assumptions and reaction definitions;
then investigate their interactions explicitly. Keep numerical residuals,
conservation, profile refinement, observed agreement and runtime scope separate.
A model may converge and still disagree with observations. A timeout is a measured
budget outcome, not evidence that the physical equations have no solution.

# Working practice

Create a study configuration, run it separately into a new directory, inspect its
results and failures, then update an analysis notebook. Render with execution
disabled. Candidate promotions should state the scientific question, exact inputs,
method, checks, uncertainty and what remains unexplained. Manuscript editing is
outside this research phase.

# Seven-state Engine calculation: numerical verification

Case 3C with ionic ePC-SAFT fugacity returns **92.08186315973761% CO2
capture**, using the pinned Engine 1.0.0 wheel from commit
`f4566b3d0c64d05822b41fe363de47ab5cfa6a0e`, SHA-256
`57bdf6c4277722fdf378107fa940fd321a4e9caeed8875165a27c318239dbd4a`.
This is numerical verification of the existing seven-state equations, not
physical validation or an isolated thermodynamic-model comparison.

The input is `C_cases_data/3C`, molar conversion, `legacy_ratio` vapor
composition and `reported_total_wet` gas flow: liquid CO2/MEA/water feeds
2.5639189042486694/10.255675616994678/81.1120360118802 mol/s; vapor
CO2/water/N2/O2 feeds 1.53499705118/1.47758972194387/15.133559109341697/
1.2841965375344333 mol/s. Liquid and vapor enter at 318.15 and 316.75 K;
packed height is 6 m, area 0.3216990877275948 m², and constant pressure
109500 Pa. The equations use legacy chemical equilibrium, empirical enthalpy
states, explicit enhancement, raw states and numerical derivatives. No
thermodynamic parameters or transport equations changed.

SciPy boundary-value collocation used 21 starting nodes, tolerance 0.5,
boundary tolerance 0.001 and at most 1000 nodes. It returned 22 nodes after
two iterations in 4.178 s within `execution.wall_limit_s = 600`.
Maximum collocation RMS residual is 0.22481082656001908; maximum scaled
boundary residual is 1.6940658945086007e-21. The separate boundary residual
percent norm is 6.915441663935132e-14. The loose collocation tolerance does
not establish profile refinement or capture accuracy.

With both stream flows represented as positive magnitudes and liquid flowing
toward decreasing height, the conserved differences are liquid minus vapor.
Maximum drift from the bottom native node is:

| Quantity | Absolute drift | Relative drift and normalization |
|---|---:|---:|
| CO2 flow difference | 4.440892098500626e-16 mol/s | 2.893094872779576e-16 / inlet vapor CO2 |
| Water flow difference | 9.242739906767383e-11 mol/s | 6.255281672241147e-11 / inlet vapor water |
| Enthalpy-flow difference | 2.905726432800293e-7 W | 6.171416760085979e-14 / maximum inlet enthalpy-flow magnitude |
| Pressure | 0 Pa | 0 / specified pressure |

The retained seven-state ionic row for 3C in
`analyses/nccc_validation/results/final/tables/raw_c_case_thermo_benchmark.csv`
reports 88.74708790292281% capture: the new result is higher by
3.334775256814794 percentage points. That row points to
`c_case_campaign_temperature_overlay_metrics.csv`. The independent check
identified that the earlier result uses `C_cases_campaign_inputs` and starts
from 51 nodes, whereas the new run uses `C_cases_data` and starts from 21.
The input differences are:

| Quantity | Earlier campaign inputs | New run inputs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Gas CO2 mole fraction | 0.093 | 0.079 |
| Vapor flow (mol/s) | 19.3746 | 19.4303 |
| Unloaded liquid/gas molar flow ratio (L/G) | 4.7170 | 4.7023 |
| Inlet vapor CO2 flow (mol/s) | 1.8018 | 1.5350 |

The independent check's current-wheel calculations assign approximately
−0.00003 percentage points to changing the starting mesh from 21 to 51 nodes.
Using the campaign inputs gives 89.967% capture, accounting for approximately
−2.114 percentage points relative to the new result. The remaining 1.220
percentage points between that current-wheel campaign calculation and the
earlier 88.747% result cannot be assigned because the earlier run's Engine
identity is not recorded. These rounded diagnostic values are reported from
the independent check; no additional column calculation was performed for
this reporting correction. The comparison does not isolate an Engine effect
or establish numerical preservation. Capture and conservation here are a few
scalar quantities, so tables state the comparison without implying a resolved
trend.

Reproduce with `uv run --frozen python src/mea_absorption_column/research.py
analyses/research_options/inputs/engine_ionic_3c.toml --run`, choosing a new
output directory. The retained result is
[attempt.json](results/runs/engine_ionic_3c_verified_20261029/attempt.json), with
[conservation and comparison values](results/runs/engine_ionic_3c_verified_20261029/conservation_comparison.json)
and [run log](results/runs/engine_ionic_3c_verified_20261029/run.log).
The balance-report command in `scripts/check_seven_state_balances.py` reads
this retained native profile without running the model. A preceding repeat
in `results/runs/engine_ionic_3c_20261029/attempt.json` returned the identical
capture and residuals in 5.372 s.

The three distinct persistent checks use both ionic and nine-species reactive
Engine fugacity: extensive-enthalpy directional differences test temperature
inversion and chain factors; prescribed fluxes test the smooth-cap derivative
across absorption and desorption; and nonzero area factors, including both
clipped limits, test material and energy scaling and conservation. These
checks establish neither native derivatives for those optional closures nor
physical accuracy. The independent check returned Supported for `471fdac`;
this reporting correction records its identified input and mesh differences.
The results have not been promoted for manuscript use.

All 18 new checks pass. Disposable mutations (a 1 K liquid-temperature
inversion error, replacing the smooth cap by a hard cap, and ignoring the
area factor) fail the corresponding checks; the retained source was not
modified for those probes. These checks expose distinct numerical errors
rather than merely exercising the selected functions.


# Configuration capability evidence — 29 October 2026

This is issue #18's first-stage capability evidence, **not physical validation**,
mesh refinement or a solver ranking. The real resolver was attempted on 13,608
combinations: 13,554 explicitly refuse and 54 resolve for bounded execution.
[Axis values and counts](results/runs/capability_20261029/resolution_summary.json)
and [every cell's first refusal reason](results/runs/capability_20261029/capability.csv.gz)
are retained. Arbitrary strings, numerical settings and study-supplied equations
are outside this finite product.

| Formulation | Thermodynamics | Film | Energy / pressure | Density | Methods |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seven-state preset | Henry, neutral, ionic, reactive-nine | Explicit or implicit enhancement | Empirical enthalpy / constant pressure | Correlation, fixed | Shooting (`single`), SciPy BVP, finite differences |
| Twelve-state preset | `reactive_epcsaft`: nine-species liquid and neutral vapor | Equilibrium manifold or enhancement reference | Native total enthalpy / hydraulic pressure drop | Solved state by default; optional correlation | Trapezoidal, central, upwind CasADi/IPOPT; reduced shooting/collocation refuse at execution |

Isothermal energy, other pressure equations, eNRTL and MDEA refuse. Thermodynamic
labels are formulation-specific; `casadi-ipopt` is not a method token. Density is
selected with `numerics.solver_settings.liquid_density_source`. The
[48-cell legacy menu probe](results/runs/capability_20261029/legacy_resolution.json)
also identifies frozen-film input requirements. That legacy selection requires
supplied positions, conductances and bulk fugacities; no new film was constructed.
The seven-state preset does not expose this implemented legacy option. The generic
conserved factory owns its equations and labels, requires `problem_factory`, and
exposes trapezoidal, central, shooting and collocation, but not upwind.

All workers run under `nice -n 10` with the pinned Engine 1.0.0 commit
`f4566b3d0c64d05822b41fe363de47ab5cfa6a0e`, wheel SHA-256
`57bdf6c4277722fdf378107fa940fd321a4e9caeed8875165a27c318239dbd4a`.
Seven-state SciPy starts at 11 nodes, tolerance 0.5, boundary tolerance 0.001,
at most 1000 nodes, raw enthalpy states and numerical derivatives. Other
seven-state methods retain their configured grid; their preset does not expose an
11-node mesh. The wall limit is 60 s. Twelve-state methods use 11 uniform nodes,
9 film quadrature points, tolerance 1e-7 and a 180 s wall limit. The
[execution log](results/runs/capability_20261029/run.log) and numbered directories
retain requests, returned values, failures, source/wheel identities and residuals.
Wall times describe budgets on a shared desktop, not a performance comparison.

Seven-state inputs are `C_cases_data/3C`, mole conversion, `legacy_ratio` vapor
composition and reported-total-wet gas flow, detailed above. Twelve-state inputs
are `analyses/bvp_solution_methods/input/case_3c.json`: liquid feeds
2.4323205276/9.7292821105/76.9751925073 mol/s and vapor feeds
1.6540435157/1.5624169375/14.5306833586/1.6006872733 mol/s, at 318.15/316.75 K,
with bottom pressure 110900 Pa. These input bases and formulations differ;
capture differences cannot isolate a solver or film effect. Estimated mobilities,
provisional calorics and coarse meshes limit physical interpretation. Solved-state
density is about 11% high against Amundsen 2009, lowering calculated 3C holdup by
12–16% ([density study](../liquid_density/notebook.qmd)); no hydraulic accuracy is
claimed. HSL, a collection of Fortran codes for large-scale scientific computation.
https://www.hsl.rl.ac.uk/

## Corrected refusals and remaining restrictions

The Engine fugacity guard previously substituted Henry fugacities on errors.
The retained #52 attempt has zero invalid states/penalties. Its instrumented replay
returned 92.08186315973761% capture with zero substitutions. The instrumented
307-test suite recorded one substitution: neutral Engine, liquid temperature 50 K,
and NaN vapor composition. The corrected guard raises `CapabilityRefusal` with
the state and original error; the outer balance guard preserves it. The final #52
replay returns the identical capture and boundary residual,
6.915441663935132e-14 percent-norm. See [counts and conditions](results/runs/capability_20261029/guard_measurement.json).
Henry remains an explicit selection; refusals do not increment substitution counts.

Rejected implicit-enhancement subsolves previously became balance penalties. The
initial Henry shooting probe reported completion and 99.99885861038491% capture
after five penalties: a retained false success. The corrected probe refuses at
normalized height 0.07, with subsolve residual 219.496 against the unchanged 1e-6
limit. The refusal names the subsolve and physical state: four component flows
(mol/s), two enthalpy flows (W) and pressure (Pa). Film equations are unchanged.
Separately labelled strict attempts supersede affected probes in the matrix.

The legacy menu now refuses unconsumed energy, pressure and density selectors and
unknown enhancement types. Staged pumparound requires explicit
`thermal_state_mode = "temperature"`. The calculation test and CLI example now
select it; no standalone tracked intercooler study was found. None of the 69
tracked `attempt.json`/`resolved_config.json` files records a pumparound selection
that would newly refuse replay. The K3 before/after native arrays are identical:
both fail with a singular Jacobian, 95% initial capture iterate and 1542 penalties.
This preserves a failed attempt, not a converged intercooler prediction
([comparison](results/runs/capability_20261029/intercooler_comparison.json)).

One persistent independence check changes thermodynamics while preserving case,
film, energy, pressure, initialization, numerics and execution choices; only the
related Engine requirement changes. Existing generic numerical trial-state penalty
checks remain. The twelve-state feed-matched seed, 0.97 packing void fraction,
293.15–393.15 K temperature interval and fixed scales remain explicit restrictions
for #19/#31. General trial-state penalties remain; affected failed cells are
identified rather than treated as clean model predictions.

The [historical inventory](results/runs/capability_20261029/historical_penalties.json)
finds positive penalty counts in 12 initializer files and 3 diagnostic logs.
Their hashes remain unchanged; none was rerun. A seed count alone does not show
that its later reactive solution used penalties. The [initial matrix inventory](results/runs/capability_20261029/retained_penalties.json)
also preserves affected new probes. Independent review and investigator promotion
remain with the issue owner.
